title: Adaptive Kernel Profiler and Heuristic Synthesizer for Mixed-Length Workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build an adaptive, low-regret system that profiles per-architecture and per-sequence-length kernel performance, synthesizes a compact heuristic, and exposes a safe rollout path for production. We must consider prefill vs decode divergence, KV cache memory constraints, and cross-GPU heterogeneity (A100/H100 + future SKUs). This ticket covers the design, microbenchmark harness, metric definitions, initial autotuner prototype, and rollout/runbook for canary-ing changes on Dedicated clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Automated profiler generates representative cost/latency curves for at least 4 kernel implementations across 3 seq-len buckets (<=64, 65-512, >512) on A100 and H100 within 24 hours of a profiling run.

Heuristic synthesizer outputs a compact rule-set (<= 12 rules) that when applied reduces p95 token-latency on mixed-length internal benchmark by >= 12% versus current baseline without increasing p50 by >5%.
Fallback rate (instances where synthesized rule is overridden by safe fallback) < 0.5% over a 48-hour canary run on Dedicated capacity.
Cost-per-token for the mixed-length benchmark does not increase by more than 3% versus baseline (account for batching benefits).
Documentation: design doc, microbench instructions, and runbook are published and linked; PR with automated tests merged and deployed to staging.
steps: Design phase: define seq-len buckets, architecture fingerprints, and profiling methodology (microbench + sampled production traces).
Implement microbench harness that runs kernels across varying batch sizes, seq-lens, and kv-cache states on target GPUs and stores results to perf-store.
Prototype synthesizer: combine a bandit-style exploration policy for online refinement with deterministic rules for latency-critical paths.
Integrate with runtime: expose kernel-choice hook and safety envelope checks (memory guardrails, latency SLO predictions).
End-to-end canary: deploy to a small Dedicated pool, collect telemetry, validate acceptance criteria, then expand rollout.
progress_updates: 2026-02-20 - Aisha: Kickoff meeting with infra and serving teams. Aligned on seq-len buckets and initial GPU targets (A100/H100).

2026-02-25 - Marco: Microbench harness prototype committed (branch: perf/autotune-harness). Harness runs basic per-kernel timing and logs to perf-store. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1482

2026-03-02 - Marco: First profiling sweep on staging A100 vs H100 completed. Early signal: small-seqlen (<64) favors low-overhead kernel X, long-seq (>512) favors tiled attention on H100. Shared raw CSVs in drive link.

2026-03-07 - Design review: Decided to use a hybrid approach — offline fingerprint warmstart + lightweight online bandit for rare workloads. PM (Jonas) requested stronger safety envelope and an opt-out flag for customers.
2026-03-11 - Marco: Synthesizer v0 outputs 9-rule policy. Local bench shows p95 improvement of ~14% on mixed workload, cost per token +1.1%. Preparing canary run notes.
benchmarks: Mixed synthetic workload (50% <=64, 40% 65-512, 10% >512) - baseline p95: 38ms, synthesizer v0 p95: 32.7ms (~14% improvement)
Cost delta: baseline cost-per-token $0.00090, synthesizer v0 $0.00091 (+1.1%)
Per-GPU note: H100 long-seq tiled kernel gave 20% p95 win vs default on >512 sequences in our microbench. A100 favored smaller-kernel pipelining at medium seq lengths.
rollout_plan: Stage: merge harness and synthesizer to staging, run nightly profiling sweep; smoke test with synthetic traces.
Canary: enable synthesized heuristic on a 2-node Dedicated pool limited to internal traffic for 48 hours. Observe fallback rate, tail latencies, and cost metrics.
Gradual: expand to 10% of Dedicated traffic, run 7-day validation. If acceptance criteria hold, promote to 100% Dedicated unpinned routes with a 2-week observation window.
Customer opt-out: provide route-level flag to pin kernel-selection to previous behavior until customer explicitly upgrades.
risks: Incorrect batching interaction: heuristics that favor latency may reduce batch efficiency and increase cost; mitigate by including batching-aware cost signal in objective.
KV cache memory pressure: some kernels increase working set; safety envelope must block allocations that would exceed node memory thresholds.
Model/regression risk: kernel choice could change numerical behavior for quantized kernels; require eval harness on representative prompts and regressions gating.
